title: Only 6% Of Adults Can Pass This Barrister Entrance Exam
summary: Ten questions test courtroom language, precedent, evidence and professional judgment.

landing.intro: The opening questions sound familiar. Then the exam moves into precedent, evidence and courtroom reasoning.

about.body:
This ten-question entertainment challenge uses broad concepts found across common-law legal systems in Tier 1 English-speaking countries. Exact rules and terminology vary by jurisdiction, so the questions focus on portable courtroom reasoning rather than one country’s admission syllabus.

Choose one answer for each question. Correctness stays hidden until the final reveal, where the complete answer review is available to unlock.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Answer ten increasingly difficult courtroom questions.
Choose the single best legal concept or advocacy response.
Reveal your score, then unlock every answer you missed.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not a bar admission exam, legal qualification or legal advice. Laws and professional rules vary by jurisdiction.

stage-1.preAdCopy: Your ten answers have been checked and your courtroom reasoning score is ready to reveal.

profile-1.title: The Courtroom Standout
profile-1.copy: You moved confidently from foundational principles into evidence and precedent. Even the final professional judgment question did not unsettle your reasoning.

profile-2.title: The Persuasive Advocate
profile-2.copy: You passed a challenge that catches out most adults. Your command of courtroom language and legal reasoning was consistently strong.

profile-3.title: The Sharp Case Analyst
profile-3.copy: You built a strong result across a demanding mix of legal concepts. A few finer distinctions kept the pass mark just beyond reach.

profile-4.title: The Promising Pupil
profile-4.copy: The courtroom foundations clicked, while precedent and evidence introduced harder distinctions. The review explains every missed answer.

profile-5.title: The First-Day Advocate
profile-5.copy: This exam moved rapidly into specialist language. Your strongest legal area shows where your courtroom instincts already have a foothold.

score.passed: You passed the Barrister entrance challenge!

insights.overview: Your courtroom score at a glance

barrister-q1.question: In a criminal trial, who normally bears the burden of proving the charge?

barrister-q2.question: Which principle treats an accused person as innocent unless guilt is proved?

barrister-q3.question: What is an earlier court decision that may guide a later similar case called?

barrister-q4.question: What is the questioning of a witness by the opposing side commonly called?

barrister-q5.question: What Latin term describes the legal reason essential to a court’s decision?

barrister-q6.question: What is a judicial observation that is not essential to the decision often called?

barrister-q7.question: What term commonly describes an out-of-court statement offered to prove the truth of what it says?

barrister-q8.question: Which question most clearly suggests the answer the examiner wants?
answers: The light was red when you crossed, wasn’t it?

barrister-q9.question: Judicial review is primarily concerned with which issue?
answers: Whether a public decision was made lawfully
Whether a jury chose the best witness
Whether a contract made a profit
Whether every appeal should be allowed

barrister-q10.question: Broadly, what does the cab-rank principle ask an eligible barrister to do, subject to professional rules and exceptions?
answers: Accept suitable instructions regardless of the client’s identity or the case’s popularity
